input.command: git log --oneline -20 && git status && git branch -vv && ls -la && ls -la artifacts scratch 2>/dev/null; find . -type f -not -path './.git/*' | head -100
git show --stat HEAD && git remote -v && git log --all --oneline | head -50 && node --version
git status --short && git branch -r | head -40 && git log -1 --format='%an %ae'

mkdir -p /opt/cursor/artifacts && node smoke.ts > /opt/cursor/artifacts/smoke.log && node scratch/check.ts > /opt/cursor/artifacts/checks.log && cat /opt/cursor/artifacts/smoke.log /opt/cursor/artifacts/checks.log && git rev-parse HEAD^ 2>&1 || true && git log -1 --format='%P'

cat > /opt/cursor/artifacts/code-tour-author-handoff.md << 'EOF'
<decision>
Credit authorizes goods plus the given surcharge; debit authorizes goods only, because the ticket allows the 3% surcharge on credit cards and only says debit uses this checkout. Prepaid authorizes half the goods, floored, with no surcharge, because that is the hold the ticket says checkout places and the written rule only forbids the surcharge. History is unused: nothing in the ticket changes this sale based on prior sales. I set aside recomputing 3%, capping the surcharge, and treating the half-hold as a bug to replace with the full goods amount.
</decision>
<risk>
Prepaid half versus full goods is the sharp edge: a reviewer who reads "has been authorizing half" as a bug will expect the full merchandise total. Debit is the other one: "same checkout" can be read as goods plus surcharge. Odd cent amounts floor (1001 -> 500), and a 1-cent prepaid sale authorizes 0.
</risk>
<verified>
node smoke.ts prints authorizedCents -> 0 on the neutral fixture. node scratch/check.ts passed credit 10000+300=10300, debit 10000 ignoring surcharge, prepaid 10000 -> 5000 and 1001 -> 500, and the zero, negative, unknown-card, and history cases.
</verified>
EOF
git add impl.ts artifacts && git commit -m "Implement ticket" && git push -u origin HEAD && git status
